prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (within 500 words)

- Economy and jobs: Invest in renewable energy, home insulation and green infrastructure; responsible fiscal rules; improve trade with Europe, including veterinary/plant health and mutual recognition agreements; expand the British Business Bank; financial inclusion duties for regulators; priority future tax cut via higher personal allowance; raise revenue by increasing the Digital Services Tax to 6%, reforming capital gains, a 4% levy on large share buybacks, a windfall tax on oil and gas, and reversing bank tax cuts. Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; industrial strategy with R&D to 3–3.5% of GDP; AI regulatory framework; late-payment enforcement; replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants; new National Colleges; living wage review; Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; modernise gig-economy rights; fix Statutory Sick Pay.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% electricity from renewables by 2030; 10‑year home energy upgrade (free for low-income households), social energy tariff, decouple electricity from gas prices; zero‑carbon new homes; rooftop solar incentives; maintain fracking ban and ban new coal mines; end fossil fuel subsidies with a just transition; expand storage and interconnectors; support community energy; associate UK ETS with the EU; corporate net-zero duties; Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism; support CCS and low‑carbon industry.

- Health and care: Right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent) with 8,000 more GPs; restore NHS dentistry access; youth mental health hubs and school professionals; cancer treatment start within 62 days; public health investment; independent pay review and long-term workforce plan; reduce ambulance handover delays; invest in hospital estate; patient charter and digital interoperability; faster access to novel medicines; shift drugs policy toward health, including a regulated cannabis market; fair hospice funding. Social care: free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College, carer minimum wage (+£2/hour); cross‑party funding settlement; paid carers’ leave and regular respite; National Care Agency; digital and independent living strategies.

- Education and families: Mental health professional in every school; per‑pupil funding rises and school repairs; tutoring guarantee; early years boost and higher pupil premiums; restore maintenance grants; Lifelong Skills Grants; teacher recruitment/retention plan; curriculum and Ofsted reform; stronger SEND funding and national body; Erasmus+ return. Families and welfare: extend free school meals to all children in poverty; overhaul parental leave (day‑one rights, higher pay, extra partner month); target to end deep poverty; remove two‑child limit and benefit cap; five‑day wait for Universal Credit; protect pensions with the triple lock; improve disability benefits and Carer’s Allowance.

- Housing and communities: Build 380,000 homes a year (150,000 social), new garden cities, brownfield with affordable quotas, reform land compensation, use‑it‑or‑lose‑it permissions; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions, three‑year default tenancies, landlord register; remove cladding at no leaseholder cost; rent‑to‑own for social housing; end rough sleeping and scrap the Vagrancy Act; local powers over second homes/short lets; universal gigabit; stronger local climate powers.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout, restore 2030 ZEV mandate, plug‑in grant, 5% VAT on public charging; rail fare freeze and simplification; new Railway Agency; major electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail, accessibility upgrades; bus franchising powers and £2 cap while fares reviewed; national active travel strategy; shift road funds to maintenance; aviation tax reform, super tax on private jets, limit short domestic flights where rail <2.5 hours; moratorium on airport expansion pending a national framework.

- Environment, food and farming: Tough sewage plan (new regulator powers, public‑benefit water companies, binding targets), real‑time spill data, social water tariff; double nature by 2050, 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and Air Quality Agency; deposit return scheme and phase‑out of non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; 30% land/sea protection by 2030; strong biodiversity net gain; £1bn/yr for Environmental Land Management; fair trading standards in deals; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator; support alternative proteins; comprehensive animal welfare bill.

- Crime and rights: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance for burglaries; invest to clear court backlogs; rehabilitation focus; Online Crime Agency; replace Police and Crime Commissioners with local boards; domestic abuse specialists; halve offence‑to‑sentencing times; youth diversion; anti‑fraud measures; modern slavery protections. Uphold the Human Rights Act and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; ban conversion practices; revise protest and surveillance laws; flexible work rights; stronger support for survivors; diversity and disability employment measures; assisted dying free vote.

- Political system: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap political donations; ministerial code in law; reform the Lords; written federal constitution and deeper devolution; citizens’ assemblies; transparency for lobbying and digital campaigning; protect the Electoral Commission; whistleblower office; Hillsborough Law.

- Immigration and asylum: End hostile environment; move work/student visa policy out of the Home Office; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; three‑month asylum decision service standard and work rights after three months; flexible work visa system and expanded Youth Mobility; fair family visa rules; settled status safeguards; lower child citizenship fees; expand safe and legal routes; end child detention; 28‑day detention limit.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; parliamentary votes on military action; stricter arms export controls; fix procurement; stronger support for service personnel and veterans; deepen European defence cooperation and Five Eyes ties. Restore 0.7% aid with poverty focus; support Ukraine (including seizing frozen Russian assets); rebuild European partnerships via staged roadmap; promote human rights, recognise Palestine, pursue ceasefire and two‑state solution, support BNOs, oppose abuses in Xinjiang, and expand BBC World Service.
